Failures:

* Did not carb-load like I had planned

Exercises:

* Squat: 145 lbs - 5x5 * OHP: 55 lbs - 5x5 * Deadlift: 175 lbs - 5

Milestone Evaluation:

I did the Half Mudder. I finished every obstacle minus one which was closed due to lightning. I am pretty proud of myself for being able to complete the course without feeling too bad at the finish. There are no clocks around and I didn't wear a watch so I don't know how long I actually took to finish the course. However, some obstacles had a wait for them and for some of the team based ones, I stuck around a little bit after to help others complete the obstacle. Some of the toughest obstacles were climbing ones like trying to get over two 9ft walls when your feet are too muddy to be any help. Other obstacles weren't as tough, like crawling under a cargo net or carrying a person 100 feet. There was also plenty of areas with mud or muddy water that really slows you down. The organizers also make a point to say that its not a race but a challenge. I still would have liked to know my time, but if the course was timed then a lot people probably wouldn't help out at the team obstacles. I jogged a lot of the terrain between the obstacles when I could. Part of the course would go through a creek bed or a pond where jogging was impractical. I felt pretty good after finishing but after waking up the next day, I was sore all over and had scratched my knees up too. Most of the soreness is in my abdominal region.

I never did run this week. I forgot my running shoes when I went to the gym and then when I planned to go later, a storm came in and I stayed at home instead. I will make an attempt later this week when I am healed up from the Half Mudder, just to see how well I can do.

Now that the Half Mudder is over, I don't have any concrete goals right now. I would like to have a visible six pack but that is subjective and is hard to measure. I plan to begin eating at a surplus after Memorial day to put on muscle mass so I might come up with goals of being able to lift a certain weight or have X% increase over a baseline over a few months.

I am proud of myself for being able to complete the course and for losing all the fat that I have. I would like to thank everyone who has given me advice and support this year. This has been an amazing year so far, I can't wait to see what i am capable of accomplishing the rest of this year.

Make a disk image backup. Now.

Not just an ordinary backup, a disk image backup. It gives you a good last-resort option if the worst happens. You'll want to buy an external hard drive to put it on that's at least slightly bigger than your current hard drive, because it will be, byte-for-byte, a perfect copy of your current hard drive.

If Windows 10 happens, then take your changed/added files, put them on another drive (be sure you get all of them), and then restore the disk image backup. Your computer will be just like it was on the day you made the imaging.

Note that it is best if you have someone actually guide you through this in person if at all possible. I would not trust the Geek Squad to do it, though chances are a competent mom-and-pop type store could pull it off with no troubles, and there are better guides online if you have no idea of what I'm babbling about. Nevertheless, this is probably the best way to make sure your software will survive.
You can make images that are not byte-for-byte. CloneZilla is a decent tool for making such an image but it will only take about as much space as you have data (plus OS & filesystem info size).
